chapter: Los Angeles, Ellington and the recording scene
title: First encounter with Louis Armstrong in Los Angeles, 1937
summary: He replaces Pops Foster for several weeks in Louis Armstrong's band with Luis Russell, earning $85 a week.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Okay, I have to. Because before that.. When I mentioned Elmer Fain it makes me think of my first encounter with Louis Armstrong, which was on the 13th of November, 1937. I guess I was still a teenager. Anyhow, Pops Foster got sick, and I guess I was new in town then... Anyhow, Elmer Fain said, "Hey, kid, I got a job for you." I said, "What?" He said, "Louis Armstrong needs a bass player." So they were playing at the Vogue Ballroom on 9th and Grand in Los Angeles. You may remember that, too. But anyhow, they were playing, and I went with the band making $85 a week. This was the day after I had bought one of the same basses I have now. Luis Russell was the bandleader, and in the band was Paul Barbarin, Red Allen, Charlie Holmes, and Luis Russell playing piano -- and naturally Pops. I think Pops was 36 or 37 at the time. I was there when he married Lucille, too.
No, there's a lot I don't know!
Anyhow, that was one of the thrills of my life. We had the white (?) uniforms and making $85 a week; I'd never heard of that kind of money!
Oh, that was good. Awfully good.

Oh, that was great. Well, I think I stayed there a month or six weeks, then Pops Foster came back, and I resumed my... I can call it a "career" now, although at the time I was just having fun. I was determined to be a good musician.
